write_authority: none — this module persists NOTHING. ChatEngine owns the transport and the prefs (§10.1).
failure_modes: no chat engine -> enteredTab reports sent:false, canFollow reports false, health says 'no-chat-engine'
partner not sharing their tab -> follow() refuses, naming the reason
no tab seen yet -> follow() refuses
presence older than 12s -> reported stale, line disappears
listener throws -> named in console, presence keeps working
invariants: NOTHING IS PERSISTED — not the follow state, not who was where, not for how long. health().persisted is structurally 0 and a test drives 200 tab moves to prove the store stays empty.
you can only follow someone already sharing their tab — which was already opt-in and two-sided
following BROADCASTS presence:follow — a follow the other person cannot see is surveillance, not co-navigation
being followed is REPORTED, never asked for: a follow that could sit hidden while pending is worse than one stated plainly
either side ends it alone — the follower by unfollowing, the followed by turning tab sharing off
a follow NEVER steals focus mid-sentence: it defers while a text field holds content, retries, and is cancelled by unfollow
an empty text field is not typing; a checkbox or button focus is not typing
design_decision: Following someone through an app is one step from watching them. The asymmetry is closed deliberately rather than left to trust: the follow is announced, and both sides can end it unilaterally. §17.3 — recorded, not buried.
status: implemented — 18/18 in test/presence.test.mjs. Suite 169/169 + lints. Two-device verification remains open by design.
